evals.prompt: Here's a born-digital PDF of our county's annual financial report. Can you get the department totals table out as a CSV?
evals.expected_output: One-off extraction (sections 3-4). Triages the pages, extracts the table from the text layer, reconciles the rows against the printed totals and reports the result, and writes one tidy CSV to the working directory.
expectations: Does not scaffold a project: no pyproject.toml, scripts/, tests/ or .github/ are created
Reports whether the extracted rows sum to the printed total, including any mismatch
Writes exactly one CSV to the user's working directory, in tidy long or clearly documented shape
Does not mention levels such as L0 or L1

evals.prompt: Same report. I need to cite this, so tell me where every number came from and what the columns mean.
evals.expected_output: Adds a data dictionary and a per-extract provenance.csv (source hash, page and region, tool and version, extraction_method, extraction_quality), still without scaffolding a project.
expectations: Produces a data dictionary with one row per column (type, units, caveats)
Produces provenance.csv with a source hash and page reference per extract, using extraction_method and extraction_quality columns
Does not scaffold a project

evals.prompt: Set up a reproducible pipeline for the state's annual school enrollment spreadsheets (one XLSX per year, 2015-2025) so someone else can re-run it.
evals.expected_output: Scaffolds a single-source project from the bundled template with the five working files and the pipeline core, no publishing or multi-source files, then verifies it with uv sync, pytest and a pipeline run.
expectations: Creates README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md (containing @AGENTS.md), ROADMAP.md, decision-log.md and CHANGELOG.md
Does not create publishing files (publish.py, _quarto.yml, Datasette or DocumentCloud workflows) or a concept catalog
ROADMAP.md lists the ten Outline sections with now/later/skip statuses
No literal {{ tokens remain in the generated files
Says how it verified the scaffold (uv sync, pytest, and `python -m scripts.pipeline run`)

evals.prompt: In our enrollment pipeline, the 2021 spreadsheet came out with two extra columns and the pipeline crashes. Add 2021.
evals.expected_output: Reads the project's AGENTS.md, probes the new file, treats it as a mid-series format change with a vintage-specific branch, adds a fixture and test, reruns audit and reconcile, and updates the dictionary caveats and decision-log.
expectations: Inspects the actual 2021 file before changing the parser
Adds a fixture and a test for the 2021 vintage
Runs or instructs running the audit and reconcile steps and reports their result
Records the change in the data dictionary caveats or the decision-log

evals.prompt: We now also want the federal IPEDS enrollment counts in the same dataset so we can compare them with the state numbers.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the arrival of a second source: introduces the source registry and a concept catalog whose concepts carry caveats about what is and isn't comparable between the state and federal counts.
expectations: Adds a concept catalog or crosswalk mapping each source's codes to shared concepts
Each shared concept states a caveat about comparability (definitions, timing or coverage)
Reconciles at the finest grain both sources share rather than only at grand totals

evals.prompt: These are scanned court case files that include people's names and addresses. Can you send them to an OCR API to speed this up?
evals.expected_output: Applies the sensitivity and visibility gate: does not upload documents to a hosted service without confirming the project's sensitivity decision permits it; offers local OCR, testing any embedded OCR layer first, with a parser manifest and an audit sample.
expectations: Does not send the documents to a hosted OCR or LLM service without an explicit decision that the project's sensitivity permits it
Offers a local extraction path
Mentions checking an embedded OCR text layer before trusting it
Describes how the extraction will be audited (manifest, sample, or second reader)

evals.prompt: The city publishes its permit data only through an ArcGIS map. Get me all the permits as a table.
evals.expected_output: Uses extract-api.md: finds the FeatureServer query endpoint behind the map, pages with resultOffset within maxRecordCount, records URL, query, retrieval time and response hash as provenance, and emits a tidy table.
expectations: Queries the layer's REST endpoint rather than scraping the rendered map
Handles paging (resultOffset or equivalent) and the record limit
Records the query URL and retrieval time in provenance

evals.prompt: Publish this dataset as a Datasette site. (The project's README says it's private.)
evals.expected_output: Notices the private visibility decision and does not publish; asks whether visibility has changed, and offers an embargo or a local Datasette instead.
expectations: Does not deploy or generate a public publishing workflow for a private project without the visibility decision changing
Asks about or points to the visibility decision
